reconciliation

rek-un-sil-ee-AY-shun — a long word; break it into 're-concile-ation,' coming back together again. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Reconciliation is the act of restoring friendly relations after a disagreement or estrangement.

After years of not speaking, the brothers' tearful reconciliation surprised the whole family.

Example

Two childhood best friends stop speaking after a painful argument. Years later, one reaches out with an honest apology. Their reconciliation begins over coffee, as they talk through what happened and slowly start calling each other again.

Together they are restoring the friendship after the falling-out. Unlike 'forgiveness,' which is a private feeling one person can offer alone, reconciliation is the mutual, shared process of rebuilding the relationship itself.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

reunion: A reunion is the coming back together after time apart — a family reunion, classmates meeting again — and it says nothing about any quarrel. A reconciliation is needed only when something went wrong: it is the repair of a relationship after a falling-out, not just a gathering.

peacemaking: Peacemaking is the work of getting two hostile sides to stop fighting, often done by a third party standing between them. Reconciliation is what the two sides themselves finally reach: the actual restoring of friendly relations, not the effort of brokering it.

settlement: A settlement is a resolution that officially ends a dispute — terms are agreed, papers are signed, the argument is over. A reconciliation goes further than ending the quarrel: it restores the friendship itself. Two sides can settle a lawsuit and still refuse to speak.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

estrangement: a state of being distant or alienated

feud: a long, bitter quarrel

Where it sits · how fully the relationship is repaired

truce → reconciliation → healing

truce vs. reconciliation: A truce is weaker than a reconciliation — a truce just pauses the fighting, while a reconciliation actually restores the friendly relationship itself.

healing vs. reconciliation: Healing can be stronger than reconciliation: a reconciliation restores the relationship, but full healing means every bit of old hurt has faded, not just the conflict itself.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — re-: again (Latin)

Root — concil: to bring together (from Latin conciliare, 'to bring together, to unite')

Suffix — -iation: act or process of (Latin -atio; the linking -i- joins the root to the suffix)

Put it together: Re- ('again') + concil ('to bring together' — from Latin conciliare) + -iation ('act or process of'): a reconciliation is the act of bringing people back together again after they have drifted apart.

Use the root in a new word: council: Reporters described the ambassador's second speech as strikingly conciliatory.
